R. & Regs. r. 560-7-4-.02**: *"Only retirement income that is included in Georgia taxable income shall be included when computing the retirement income exclusion."* **⚠⚠ THE REPORTED CAUSE IS CONFIRMED AND THE REPORTED ANSWER IS REFUTED — by the packet's own federal forms.** Filed spouse RIE of $7,672 is not reachable by any correct computation: Form 8582 Part VIII shows the loss **allowed $0**, Schedule E line 41 is the taxpayer's −$2,948 alone, and **there is no $2,948 of spouse partnership INCOME anywhere on the return**. ## 🟢 **s241 (2026-08-10 — 1040 LANE: BATCH-004 #7 AND BATCH-003 #2 BUILT TOGETHER — they were ONE section, and a duplicate row made tax VANISH)** (one deploy; `97ea4a5`; migration **0278**). Two batch items, one build. #7 asks for Form 5329 **Part III** (traditional-IRA excess carryovers) and #2 for **Part VII** (HSA excess) — and s240 had already established they are the SAME `_excess_part()` helper inside one function, differing only in which model fields feed it. Both are refuted as stated and real as LANE gaps: `Form5329` has carried every Parts I-IX leaf since migration 0119, `compute_5329_full` computes all nine parts, and `compute_5329_db` has routed both owners' totals ONCE to Schedule 2 line 8 → line 21 → 1040 line 23 all along. Built `form_5329s` carrying the preparer-keyed leaves of **all nine parts**, not only the two asked for — a partial allowlist would leave the rest un-importable for no reason. Two design calls stated rather than implied: **`owner` is REQUIRED**, unlike its Form 8606 sibling, because compute pairs each row with THAT owner's early-distribution 1099-Rs, so a spouse's form landing on the model default absorbs the wrong person's Part I line 1 while the real spouse row goes missing; and **Part I line 1 plus every subtotal are refused BY NAME** (the s238 column-(a) doctrine) because a bare "unknown field" reads as a typo and invites hunting for the right spelling of something that must not exist. **⚠⚠ THE FINDING THAT GENERALIZES: A DICT KEYED BY A ROW ATTRIBUTE MAKES DUPLICATES VANISH, NOT DOUBLE.** `compute_5329_db` and the diagnostics' `_f5329_state` both do `{r.owner: r for r in Form5329.objects.filter(...)}` — an ordinary, readable line that silently encodes a uniqueness contract the database never enforced. A second row for the same owner does not double-count: **the last one wins and every earlier row's additional tax is dropped**, with no error, no diagnostic and no rendered form. **Measured before the fix with a throwaway probe**: a taxpayer row with $1,840 of prior traditional-IRA excess plus a second taxpayer row with $250 of prior HSA excess wrote Schedule 2 line 8 = **$15.00 instead of $125.40**. *When compute reduces a row SET to a dict keyed by one field, that key IS a uniqueness constraint — and if the DB does not have it, the overflow is invisible rather than wrong.* The contrast is the tell: this form's own siblings `Form8606` and `HSAAccount` ITERATE their rows, so a duplicate there at least surfaces as a double count someone would notice. ⚠ **Sign: UNDERSTATES tax**, the direction nobody reports. Closed on every write path — migration 0278 (`uniq_form5329_owner_per_return`, with the shared DB checked first: no existing duplicates), a named 400 on the browser POST **and on the re-owner PATCH**, and a staging error that names the replacement instead of dying on an IntegrityError mid-commit. ⚠ An independent confirmation nobody had connected: **`ReturnData1040.xsd` caps `IRS5329` at maxOccurs 2** — the schema has said "one per owner" all along. **⚠ THE SECOND FINDING: A FORM LINE THAT NAMES ITS OWN SOURCE IS TELLING YOU WHAT TO RECONCILE.** Line 44 reads on the printed 2025 face *"2025 distributions from your HSAs **from Form 8889, line 16**"* — the TAXABLE portion, so a fully qualified distribution puts -0- there. BATCH-003 #2's packet has a fully qualified **$631** distribution, which is exactly why its $250 excess survives to line 46 and carries its $15; **keying the $631 gross wipes out both, and nothing visible changes on the face because the part just prints as zero.** New **`D_5329_006`** runs that sentence as a reconciliation, erroring in BOTH directions, matching by owner, and staying quiet where the return carries no HSA (the `D_8889_*` family owns that gap). ⛔ Line 36 says the same thing about **Form 8853 line 8 and CANNOT be reconciled — there is no `Form8853` model at all**; logged in DEFERRAL_AUDIT, and it gives the long-passed-over **Form 8853 Section C** build a second reason to happen (Sections A/B are its near neighbour). **"Carry remaining excess forward" is built too**, per #7's ask: each part's total-excess line becomes next year's prior-excess line in the face's own words (line 9 = "line 16 of your 2024 Form 5329"; likewise 24→18, 32→26, 40→34, 48→42), the producer reusing `compute_5329_form_lines` so the carried figure cannot drift. **Part VIII (ABLE) is deliberately absent** — its face is line 50 alone with no prior-year line, so the form provides no chain, and whether an uncorrected ABLE excess is taxed again is a §529A question the FORM does not answer; agenda'd for RS rather than guessed, with a test pinning the omission. Answer keys **hand-derived from the printed face**: #7 line 13 = 0, line 14 = 1,840, line 16 = 1,840, line 17 = 6% × 1,840 = 110.40 → Schedule 2 line 8 **110**; #2 line 45 = 0, line 46 = 250, line 48 = 250, line 49 = **15.00**. Both tie end to end through staging and commit. Also retired **three stale hand-counted literals** found in passing: the two `D_RET_` registration counts (**RED since s239 added D_RET_011 without re-pinning them** — shipped unnoticed) now read the roster from `RULES_RETIREMENT`, and the proforma producer's key-contract guard had never gained `_k1_basis_704d` (s228) or `_carryforward_attributes` (s235) and was passing only because its fixture emits neither — *a drift guard that passes by absence is not guarding anything*. 48 tests; flow assertions 526; a 685-test targeted sweep green but for four known reds (3 × the s225 `--reuse-db` cleanup class, 1 × the s233 `inspect.getsource` false-red, **now its FIFTH consecutive session — it should stop being deferred**). ⚠ MOVEMENT: **none** — no compute changed, rows only exist where a payload or preparer creates one, `D_5329_006` fires only where a 5329 row and an HSA already disagree, and the roll-forward touches only a NEW year's return. **BATCH-004 and BATCH-003 both stay in the queue** with result annexes — eight and six items respectively are genuine builds.

## 🟢 **s241b (2026-08-10 — 1040 LANE: BATCH-004 #6 BUILT — and the constraint added HOURS EARLIER would have been a DEFECT here)** (one deploy; `d55ff15`; no migration). Refuted as stated, real as a lane gap: "the current `backentry.v1` schema explicitly leaves Form 8863 and education-credit inputs unsupported" is true of the IMPORT LANE only. `EducationStudent` has existed since migration 0071 (the `dependent` FK since 0093), and `compute_8863`, `f8863_2025.py`, the `IRS8863` MeF document, `rules_8863.py` and `seed_form_8863.py` are all complete — the credit, the $4,000 cap, the MAGI phaseout, the four-year limit and the refundable split were never the gap. Built `education_students`: one row per Part III student, who may be the taxpayer, the spouse or a dependent (which is why it is its own family and not a flag on `dependents`). **⚠⚠ THE FINDING WORTH CARRYING IS A NEGATIVE ONE, AND IT IS THE MIRROR OF s241's.** s241 had just closed a Form 5329 hole where `compute_5329_db` reduced its rows to `{r.owner: r for r in …}`, so a duplicate row VANISHED — fixed with a DB uniqueness constraint. The obvious next move was to look for the same shape here and add the same constraint. **It would have been a defect.** `compute_8863` does `list(EducationStudent.objects.filter(...))` and ITERATES, and Parts I/II aggregate across students (L1 = Σ line 30, L10 = Σ line 31), so several students on one return is the *normal* case and a uniqueness rule would have destroyed the multi-student return outright. *The transferable rule is NOT "add the constraint" — it is **read what the consumer does with the row set, every time**. A dict-by-attribute is a uniqueness contract; a list is not; and the two are one character apart at the call site.* Pinned two ways: a test asserts no `uniq` constraint sits on the model, and another asserts `compute_8863_db` still iterates — so a future refactor to a dict fails loudly instead of silently dropping a student's credit. **⚠ SECOND FINDING: `student_name` / `student_ssn` are STORED ON THE ROW, not derived from the `dependent` link** — the renderer, three `rules_8863` messages and BOTH MeF paths read them off the row, and `read_model` raises `UnmappableValue` on a student missing a name or 9 SSN digits, so a row without them is **un-transmittable**, not merely untidy. Both required on every row, dependent students included. **The student-to-dependent link** (the leg the item names) uses the `misc_1099s.link_key` carrier shape: `dependent_key`, matched at commit by full name or by SSN compared digits-only, REQUIRED when `owner` is "dependent" and REJECTED for a taxpayer or spouse student. ⚠ An unmatched key commits **UNLINKED with a warning** rather than refusing, and the sign was checked before choosing: the credit is unaffected and `rules_8863` still reports on the student in full (its list is unfiltered) — what is lost is `credit_gates.d_credit_aotc`, whose `_aotc_claiming_students` filters `dependent__isnull=False`. **Diagnostic specificity, not money.** Guessing a dependent would attribute one child's education credit to another in the diagnostics, which reads as fact. Two refusals moved to STAGING rather than after commit: a student carrying BOTH credits (§25A(c)(2)(A) makes them mutually exclusive per student per year, and the packet can only show one, so catching it while the packet is open beats `D_8863_DUAL_STUDENT` afterwards), and the computed lines **BY NAME** — including the Parts I/II aggregates, which cannot sit on a single student row at all. **Answer key hand-derived from the statute**: §25A(b)(1) = 100% of the first $2,000 + 25% of the next $2,000, so $4,000 → **$2,500**; §25A(i) makes 40% refundable → **$1,000**, leaving **$1,500**. Matches the filed packet exactly; verified end to end onto 1040 line 29 and Schedule 3 line 3. Also pinned: two students aggregating to $5,000 (the case a constraint would have broken), and an eligibility answer routing a student off the AOTC to the LLC — which is why the four line 23-26 answers must import exactly as sent. 25 tests; flow assertions 526; a 593-test sweep green but for the three known s225 `--reuse-db` cleanup reds. ⚠ MOVEMENT: **none**. **BATCH-004 stays in the queue** — 3 of 10 resolved, 7 genuine builds queued.

## 🟢 **s241g (2026-08-10 — THE `inspect.getsource` FALSE-RED CLASS IS RETIRED: 24 assertions, 24 files, 0 remaining)** (one deploy; `cdbec66`; no migration). Twenty-four assertions checked rule-registry wiring as `assert "RULES_X" in inspect.getsource(seed_builtin_rules)`. s233 refactored that function to iterate `all_registered_rules()` on 2026-08-08, so the literal left its source and **every one became a false red**. That recurring toll is why it became a unit rather than a footnote. **⚠⚠ THE CHEAP REPAIR WAS REJECTED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** `all_registered_rules()` *does* import each registry by name, so repointing the same sniff at it would have gone green in one line — and still proved nothing, because a source-text search is satisfied by the name in a comment, a docstring, or a commented-out import. **Demonstrated rather than argued**: the teeth test injected `RULES_8889 = []` into `all_registered_rules`, a line that CONTAINS the literal `"RULES_8889"` — so a repointed sniff would have PASSED while the family reached neither the seeder nor the database. The new `tests/registry_asserts.assert_registry_wired()` resolves the named registry to its defining module and asserts every code it DECLARES is returned by `all_registered_rules()` (the function the seeder and the deploy-time system check both consume); it failed on the injected defect with *"RULES_8889 … is NOT wired into all_registered_rules() — 8 of 8 codes never reach the seeder"*, naming them. *A test that searches for a NAME proves the name exists; only a test that follows the VALUE proves the wiring.* ⚠ It asserts against what the module DECLARES, never a hand count — s239 shipped two stale counts exactly that way and s241 had to retire them. The sweep was scripted with exact-string matching that reported every file and refused what it did not recognise (17 one-line form; 7 flagged and found to be a two-line variant, one of them asserting two registries at once), and the diff was reviewed before any test ran. **Result: `-k "diagnostic"` is now 900 passed, 0 failed.**

## 🟢 **s241h (2026-08-10 — Form 8862 Parts III and IV PRINT, and I audited my own guard before trusting it)** (one deploy; `5940233`; no migration). Parts III (12-17) and IV (18-19) were TRANSMITTED but printed blank, so a preparer reviewing the paper saw empty per-child grids while the e-filed version asserted specific answers — **and the paper is what they sign**. Field map 16 → 87 entries. The render feed **mirrors `build_irs8862` deliberately** (same `classify_dependent_ctc`, same CTC-vs-ODC split, same caps, same `citizenship_status` for line 17, same eligibility trio for 19a) because the entire point of this leg is that paper and XML cannot diverge. **⚠⚠ THE TRAP, AND WHY EVERY INDEX WAS READ OFF THE PDF: the widget numbering is NOT contiguous across lines.** Line 16's four children are `c2_11..c2_14` on one full-width row, its four OTHER DEPENDENTS are `c2_15..c2_18` on two half-width rows below, and line 17 then restarts at `c2_19`. A reader assuming "eight consecutive widgets per line" would put other-dependent 1 into **child 4's column** — a wrong Yes/No on a signed form with nothing looking out of place. Anchors: at y=444.65 the printed "Child 1..4" labels are at x=64.8/194.4/324.0/453.6 with the `c2_3..c2_6` Yes boxes at x=100.8/230.4/360.0/489.6; at y=540.65 "Other dependent 1" is at x=64.8 with `c2_15` at x=165.6. **⚠ AND THE FINDING WORTH CARRYING: I audited my own guard and it had a hole.** The per-column check re-derives each box from its printed label — but it CANNOT catch a copy-paste between two lines that share column labels, because "Other dependent 1" is printed on BOTH line 16's row and line 17's, so mapping 17 to 16's widgets would have satisfied it. Added a row-identity check (each line occupies its own row, in face order down the page) and **injected exactly that copy-paste**: it failed, naming the duplicated row. An existing `test_no_duplicate_widget_targets` caught it too — defence in depth already present. *A positional guard is only as good as the thing that distinguishes the rows; ask what your own test CANNOT see.* Gates: 601 across the four 8862 + flow suites; a **1,494-test render/e-file sweep** with only the two known pre-existing reds. ⚠ MOVEMENT: printed output only — the values were already being transmitted.

DEFERRAL_AUDIT. **⚠ THE SEVERITY WAS PROVED, NOT ASSERTED**: a two-way compute pins Schedule 1 line 26 = 8,400, 1040 line 10 = 8,400 and **AGI down by exactly 8,400**, reproducing the packet's own $98,978 → $90,578. ## 🟢 **s241l/m/n/o (2026-08-10 — ★ FORM 1099-PATR, NEW UNIT, ✅ BATCH-004 #9 COMPLETE)** (`f04d351` brief · `b4c949e` model + 8z, migrations 0281 + 0282 RLS · `a841368` lane + diagnostics · `19d9579` Georgia + CRUD). **⚠ NOT through the 404-STOP gate** — per s222 no RS spec exists for any information return, so **the IRS form IS the specification** and leg 1 was `server/specs/_1099patr_source_brief.md`, verbatim from **Rev. R. & Regs. r. 560-7-4-.02 fetched verbatim FIRST (the in-app browser again; `rules.sos.ga.gov` returns only chrome to WebFetch), because s233, s236 and s239 each found this same feed wrong a different way. **(4)(b)1**'s unearned list closes with *"and other similar income"* → UNEARNED, on worksheet **L10 "Other income (losses)"**, the line that mirrors where the income sits federally — never L7, which the 1099-DIV pull owns and would clobber. **(4)(b)1**'s EARNED list opens with *"the net business income earned by an individual from any trade or business carried on by such individual"* → a row routed to a Schedule C or F is **EARNED, not unearned, and is ALREADY in the base** through that schedule's own net profit, so **only the 8z route contributes**; feeding the others would double count AND move the amount into the capped portion. **(3)**: *"Only retirement income that is **included in Georgia taxable income**"* → the box-1 nontaxable part must not reach Georgia. **(2)**: per owner, and a 1099-PATR carries ONE recipient TIN. **⚠⚠ ADDING THE FEEDER MADE AN EXISTING, CORRECT RULE WRONG — the SEVENTH time here, and this one would have opened a NEW SILENT GAP.** The L10 derive is **partial by nature**: it knows the 1099-PATR and cannot know the rest of "other income". `D_GA500_017` asked *"is L10 blank?"*, so a return with a 1099-PATR **and** other 8-line income would have had a non-blank L10 and read as COMPLETE while its base was still short — the rule would have gone quiet on exactly the returns it exists for. ## 🟢 **s241p (2026-08-10 — FORM 4547 OPENED: the source brief and the model, built through a 404 ON PURPOSE)** (one deploy; `c113bd3`; migrations 0283 + 0284 RLS). **⚠⚠ THE 404-STOP DECISION IS THE HEADLINE.** `lookup/4547/`, `F4547`, `FORM_4547`, `8879_TA` and `8879TA` **all return 404** — Rule Studio is reachable, it simply has no spec — and nothing is cached. Built anyway, with the reasoning recorded in `server/specs/_4547_source_brief.md` so it is auditable rather than a call made in passing: **the gate's own words are *"do NOT improvise the implementation"*, and there is nothing here to improvise.** `IRS4547.xsd` puts a `<LineNumber>` on every element and contains **no amount at all** except `PriorYearAGIAmt`, a signature-authentication input rather than a tax figure — the form is identity, election and signature, with no math, no routing and no line that feeds another. And every eligibility test the item asks us to diagnose is printed **verbatim** by the IRS. **The precedent is exact: `lookup/1310/` ALSO returns 404, and s223 built Form 1310 end to end** from the IRS form + its XSD + its business rules with the reading in a source brief — and Form 1310 is a *filed* form, not an information return, so this is not the s222 carve-out being stretched but the same practice on the same kind of artifact. Form 4547 is in fact **better specified than 1310 was**, because its Instructions enumerate the conditions. Both forms are on the RS agenda regardless. **THE TAX LAW, FETCHED NOT RECALLED.** Instructions for Form 4547 (12/2025), verbatim: the pilot child must *"have been born after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2029"*, *"be a U.S. citizen"*, hold a valid SSN, be anticipated to be a qualifying child, and have had no prior pilot election processed. **⚠⚠ LINE 6 AND LINE 7 ARE DIFFERENT TESTS AND THE FORM ASKS THEM SEPARATELY** — line 6 opens the account (under 18 at year end, valid SSN issued before the election, no prior election); line 7 ADDS the birth window, citizenship and qualifying-child anticipation. **A child born in 2020 qualifies for the account and NOT for the contribution**, so collapsing them would be the s239 one-sentence-two-tests error; they are separate predicates with separate tests. ⚠ The FACE states the window as a year list (*"born in 2025–2028"*) and the INSTRUCTIONS as open boundaries — **the date form is pinned**, because a year list is exactly where an off-by-one comes from, and a throwaway teeth-check confirmed `2025-01-01` is the case that separates the two readings. ⚠ An unknown DOB and an unanswered citizenship both return **None, not False**: reporting "not eligible" for an unanswered question would talk a preparer out of a $1,000 contribution the child may be entitled to (s241c — unanswered is not No). ⚠ US citizenship here is **NARROWER than the CTC/ODC test**, which a national or a resident alien passes; every other status is tested explicitly. **⚠⚠ THE SCHEMA DECIDED TWO DESIGN QUESTIONS TASTE WOULD HAVE GOT WRONG.** `IRS4547` is `minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="unbounded"` on the return and `TrumpAccountChildInfoGrp` is `maxOccurs="100"` — so the model is REPEATABLE rather than a singleton and one document carries up to a hundred children — while the **printed face has only two child columns** and the Instructions say to attach as many copies as needed. **Print and transmit therefore have genuinely different shapes**: ⌈children/2⌉ pages, one XML document, and a renderer mirroring the two-column face would silently drop children 3+. The relationship enumeration is the XSD's, **re-derived from the schema file by the test** rather than restated, so a tax-year rollover that changes it fails there instead of at transmission; what it EXCLUDES matters, because PARENT / GRANDPARENT / AUNT / UNCLE are all valid `Dependent.relationship` values and are absent, so a mapping must be able to REFUSE — falling through to `OTHER` would assert a different fact about a person the form asks about as a child (s235 verbatim). **⚠⚠ FORM 8879-TA DOES NOT TRANSMIT, AND THE BATCH ITEM SAYS IT DOES.** The item asks to *"render and transmit both forms"*; the printed header says **_"ERO must obtain and retain completed Form 8879-TA"_**, and there is **no `IRS8879TA` element anywhere in the MeF schema set** (2025v5.3, 2025v5.4 and 2026v1.0 all searched). The IRS's own *About Form 8879-TA* page describes it as filed at the same time as the income tax return, which reads as transmission — **the face and the schema win** (s239, s241o: a summary is not the artifact). This is the position the app already takes for Form 8879 itself (*"PRINT-ONLY, ERO-RETAINED"*); the electronic mirror is the Sign Here group inside `IRS4547`. Its **Part I is a COPY** — all six lines name their own source (*"First name of Child 1 from Form 4547, line 1(a)(i)"*) and Part II's declaration swears the values came from that form — so they DERIVE and are never keyed, pinned by a test asserting the model exposes no field to key one into (s234, with s238's Form 8379 column-(a) ruling as the worked precedent). **⚠⚠ `IND-476` IS A LIVE CONSTRAINT ON A BATCH ITEM NOT YET BUILT**: *"Form 4547 must not be present in a post-original return."* **Reject, Active** — and the Instructions agree in words: *"Do not amend Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR to attach Form 4547."* **BATCH-004 #1 is the 1040-X lifecycle**, so this is pinned by a test that re-reads the business-rules CSV, ensuring #1 cannot quietly undo it and the seam is not discovered by a bounced transmission (s240: the reject list is the spec for the seam). `IND-475` is only an Alert and is pinned as such so it is never treated as a refusal. **Form 4547 has NO COMPUTE LEG and that is deliberate** — nothing on it reaches the 1040, Schedule 1, AGI or tax; inventing a linkage would be worse than none. 35 tests, **teeth proven by injection before being trusted** (s232), including a check that the "no `IRS8879TA` anywhere" assertion reads real files rather than passing by absence (s241f) — it finds `IRS4547` in six of them. A 721-test regression set green including flow assertions, plus 127 model/migration/schema tests. ⚠ MOVEMENT: **NONE** — three new tables and a pure-predicate module nothing calls yet; the migrations are additive so the s190 `db_default` trap does not apply. ⛔ **#10 IS NOT FINISHED**: lane, render (⚠ the face HAS AcroForm widgets, row-named two-per-row — verify columns POSITIONALLY, s236/s241h; and `f4547.pdf` is absent from `forms_manifest.json`), MeF (⚠ refuse on an amended return per `IND-476`; line 5 is an `xsd:choice`; lines 6/7 are `minOccurs=0` so unchecked means ABSENT, never `false`) and diagnostics all remain.

## 🟢 **s241q (2026-08-10 — FORM 4547: the LANE and the DIAGNOSTICS, legs 3 and 6 of 6)** (one deploy; `1158887`; no migration). A **parent-plus-children** lane section (the `form_1095as`/`allocations` precedent): the parent is one FILED FORM, the nested `children` list is Parts II/III, and `form_8879ta` rides as a single nested dict (the `form_7203` shape). Ordered after `dependents` because each child's `dependent_key` resolves against those rows; an unmatched key commits **UNLINKED with a warning** — the election still files (name, SSN, DOB and relationship are all on the row) and what is lost is only the pilot program's citizenship check, which is what the warning says. **⚠ Staging refuses ONLY the untransmittable** — whether a child QUALIFIES is a preparer assertion the packet shows on its face, so it is transcribed and the diagnostics speak (s222). Refused: line 5's `xsd:choice` violated (the same-address indicator beside an address, or domestic beside foreign), a US address with **no county** (`CountyNm` is NOT `minOccurs=0` in that branch of the choice), "not the same address" with no address at all, an election with no children, an unnamed responsible party, more than 100 children, and the Part I address/phone choices. **⚠⚠ FORM 8879-TA's PART I IS REFUSED BY NAME**: all six lines are copies of the Form 4547, every caption says so, and Part II swears they came from that form — keying them would be the s234 two-sources defect on a signed document (the s238 column-(a) doctrine). **⚠⚠ THE GENERATOR HAD ALREADY DRIFTED, AND `children` IS REQUIRED.** Staging validated both nested families from the moment they were written, but the published schema emitted **neither** — so a payload author could not have discovered a field the server insists on, and would have had a correct payload rejected client-side while the server accepted it. **The s227 class exactly**, and the same defect `schedule_fs.other_expenses` was (validated since s225, unemitted until batch-001 #1). Fixed, and pinned by a test that reads the **generator's own `defs`** rather than the written `.json`, so a stale artifact cannot hide it either — *and the pin is proven by history, because it fails against the code as it stood an hour earlier.* **EIGHT DIAGNOSTICS, and the shape of the whole set is that LINE 6 AND LINE 7 ARE DIFFERENT TESTS**: `D_4547_AGE` (error — the ACCOUNT test alone; an 18-year-old cannot have an account opened at all), `_PILOT` (error — the birth window, **and its message explicitly says the line 6 account election may still be correct**), `_CITIZEN` (error — narrower than CTC/ODC, which a US national or resident alien passes), `_LINK` (warning, and **only when the pilot is elected**, because otherwise the citizenship test never runs and the missing link costs nothing — no nagging), `_UNKNOWN` (info — the qualifying-child anticipation and the prior-election history are facts spanning years and taxpayers the app cannot see, so they are STATED rather than guessed; silence would imply we had checked them), `_AUTH` (error — line 6 unchecked), `_AMENDED` (error — `IND-476`, **and it says the form "can be filed at any time"** so the fix is to file separately rather than abandon the election), `_8879TA` (error — an authorization with nothing to authorize). ⚠ **Every rule that can be quiet is tested quiet as well as loud** (the s241o lesson: only the QUIET case proves a comparison is real), and an unknown DOB / unanswered citizenship are silent everywhere — an unanswered question is not a failed test and the sign runs against the taxpayer. ⚠ A test pins the headline case: **a child born in 2020 gets the account and NOT the $1,000 contribution**; a rule conflating them would block a valid election AND give the wrong reason for it. 45 lane/diagnostic tests + the 35 from s241p; a 1,105-test sweep with only the three known `test_backentry_cleanup` reds. ⚠ MOVEMENT: **NONE** — every rule no-ops unless the return carries a `Form4547` row, and none exists until a preparer or payload makes one; the published-schema change is additive. ⛔ **#10 IS STILL NOT FINISHED**: the render leg and the MeF builder remain, and *duplicate child elections across two elections on one return* is named as an open item rather than left unstated.

## 🟢 **s241r (2026-08-10 — ✅✅ FORM 4547 COMPLETE: the render leg and the MeF builder, which have DIFFERENT SHAPES)** (one deploy; `e2dce0e`; no migration). **⚠⚠ PRINT AND TRANSMIT DIFFER, and that is the unit's whole risk.** The Instructions say *"If you have more than two children…attach as many copies of Form 4547 as are needed"* while `TrumpAccountChildInfoGrp` is `maxOccurs="100"` in ONE document — so **`render_4547` emits ⌈children/2⌉ pages** (concatenating across elections) while **`build_irs4547` emits ONE document carrying every child**, and both directions are pinned FACING EACH OTHER. A renderer mirroring the two-column face would silently drop children 3+ and *nothing downstream would notice*, because the XML would still carry them; a builder copying the renderer's split would produce documents the IRS reads as SEPARATE elections. The render test asserts child 3 lands in **column 1 of page 2** and that page 2 does not repeat child 1 — "present somewhere" would pass for a renderer that drifts a column per page. **⚠ THE COLUMN ASSIGNMENT WAS VERIFIED POSITIONALLY**, not by trusting the `_NN` suffix order (the s236 Form-7203 trap and the s241h guard-with-a-hole): a test reads every mapped widget's rect out of the PDF and asserts, on all **18 rows**, that child 1 is the LEFT widget in the x 260-417 band and child 2 the RIGHT in 419-576, sharing a y. **⚠ THE SIGN-HERE AND PAID-PREPARER BLOCKS ARE DELIBERATELY UNMAPPED, and that is a FINDING rather than an omission**: the taxpayer signature row carries **no widgets at all** — it is hand-signed — and the seven widgets in the preparer block were identified **from their own printed labels** (firm's name / EIN / address / phone / self-employed) rather than guessed, and are firm facts this form does not hold separately from the 1040's own preparer record; mapping them by inference would assert a wrong field on a signed consent. **MeF**: `IRS4547` sits between `IRS4255` and `IRS4562` in the ReturnData1040 sequence — after `IRS3800`, before `IRS4835` — verified against 2025v5.3, 2025v5.4 and 2026v1.0, all three agreeing, and **pinned by a test that re-derives the position from the schema file** so a tax-year rollover fails there rather than at transmission; the intra-document element order is pinned the same way (s231: an `xsd:sequence` emitter can validate BY COINCIDENCE). ⚠ Line 5's `xsd:choice` is resolved in the SOURCE dataclass so the builder never has to decide; lines 6/7 are `CheckboxType minOccurs="0"` so an unelected box is **ABSENT, never `"false"`** — which would answer a question the taxpayer did not answer on a form whose entire content is elections — and **both directions are tested**, because the absence assertion alone would pass for a builder that emitted nothing at all. **⚠⚠ THE `IND-476` REFUSAL IS BUILT**: a Form 4547 on an amended return is a hard reject whose sign is a REJECTED TRANSMISSION (every number right, the return bounces days later, no reconciliation catches it — s240), and **the message carries its remedy** because the Instructions say the form *"can be filed at any time"*, so a preparer files it separately rather than abandoning a valid election. Everything else the schema makes mandatory REFUSES rather than substituting (s241c — this is a sworn consent), and a foreign address refuses for the Form 1310 reason (no `ForeignAddressType` builder exists; inventing one for a single form is how element-order bugs get in). **⚠⚠ A TEST THAT WAS PASSING FOR THE WRONG REASON, CAUGHT AND FIXED**: the six "missing mandatory fact REFUSES" cases were green before the fixture was complete, because `extract_return` refuses on the unanswered digital-asset question long before reaching Form 4547 — so `pytest.raises(UnmappableValue)` was satisfied by an unrelated exception (**the s241f passing-by-absence trap**). The fixture now answers it and every case asserts the message is OURS; the XSD-order test had the same hazard from the other end (an empty regex match makes `[] == sorted([])` pass) and now asserts both ends non-trivial. 27 tests here; a **1,996-test sweep** across render / e-file / manifest / flow assertions with only the one known pre-existing `test_mar30_session4` red. ⚠ MOVEMENT: **NONE**, with one exception worth naming — an amended return carrying a Form 4547 now **refuses at composition** where it previously composed and would have bounced at the IRS; that reaches only returns already un-transmittable. ✅ **FORM 4547 IS COMPLETE ACROSS ALL SIX LEGS (s241p → s241r)**; Form 8879-TA stays print-only and ERO-retained by its own printed instruction. ⛔ One item ask open and NAMED: duplicate child elections across TWO elections on one return (the DB constraint is per-election).

## 🟢 **s241s (2026-08-10 — GA QEE CREDIT OPENED: the source brief, and TY2025 turns out to run TWO carryforward regimes)** (one deploy; `52c08ec`; no production code, no migration). **⚠ ANOTHER 404-STOP, built through on the s241p test.** `IT_QEE_TP2`, `IT-QEE-TP2`, `ITQEETP2`, `500_SCH2`, `GA_QEE` and `QEE` **all 404**; the `500` spec answers 200 but models only the DESTINATION — **line 21 "Total credits used from Schedule 2 (series-100)", typed `input`** — and says nothing about where that total comes from. There is nothing to improvise, because **O.C.G.A. §48-7-29.16 states every limit, the liability cap, both carryforward regimes and the no-double-benefit rule verbatim**, and the precedent is exact (`lookup/1310/` s223, `lookup/4547/` s241p). Both specs are on the RS agenda regardless. **⚠⚠ THE FINDING THAT DECIDES THE MODEL, AND THAT WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE BEEN WRONG FOR YEARS: TY2025 RUNS TWO CARRYFORWARD REGIMES SIDE BY SIDE.** The current text reads *"any unused tax credit shall be allowed the taxpayer … against up to its **succeeding three years'** tax liability"*; the pre-amendment text read *"the **succeeding five years'** tax liability"*; and the amendment note is load-bearing — **2024 Ga. Laws 598 § 1-7, eff. 1/1/2025, "app. only to unused tax credits generated during taxable years beginning on or after 1/1/2025."** So a credit generated in TY2025 carries **three** years and one generated earlier carries **five**, and **both are live in the same TY2025 return**. ⚠ A single `CARRYFORWARD_YEARS` constant is correct for one population and wrong for the other, and the error would surface **years later** when a pool expires early or late — which is why the brief specifies that **a carryover pool keys its GENERATION YEAR**, not a remaining-years counter. Both regimes were read from **primary text** (the 2024 code for the current wording, the 2022 code for the pre-amendment wording), each fetched verbatim through the in-app browser rather than taken from a search summary (s232 — a paraphrase is not a verbatim; s239 — the statute beats a stale secondary source). **⚠ VERIFY-FIRST CORRECTED THE ITEM**: GA-500 **line 21** AND Georgia Schedule 1 **line S1-5** are BOTH already seeded as preparer inputs, so the reported packet's $5,000 is **enterable today** in flattened form and that return is **not wrong**. The item's implied "cannot be represented" is not right; what flattening genuinely discards is exactly what its own second paragraph lists — the credit code, the certificate identity, generated-vs-used, the carryover and the evidentiary link between the credit and its addback. *That distinction matters, because a build that "fixes" a correct return is measuring the wrong thing.* **⚠⚠ THE SCHEDULE 1 ADDBACK IS A CONDITION ON THE CREDIT, NOT A FREE-STANDING ADDITION**: §48-7-29.16(h)(1) bars the credit for any amount *"deducted from taxable net income … as a charitable contribution"*, and `S1-5` is *"Add: **other** additions"* — a SHARED preparer line — so the build **RECONCILES** against it and never writes into it (the s230 shared-line defect, whose failure mode is a DISAPPEARED number). **⚠ THE PRE-APPROVED AMOUNT IS NOT COMPUTABLE** — the outcome of a statewide **first-come, first-served** queue against a **$120 million** annual cap that the commissioner may **PRORATE** — so it is transcribed from Form IT-QEE-TP2 and never derived. **⚠ THE REPORTED PACKET CANNOT TEST THE CAP**: MFJ with $5,000 expended is *exactly* the (b)(2) limit, so it cannot distinguish capped from uncapped, and all five of its figures being equal is a coincidence of this packet rather than a rule (s219 — a value that cancels by luck); the brief says so, so the tests that follow must use a capped case too. **⚠ (b)(3) IS AN OVERRIDE, NOT A FOURTH FILING STATUS** — *"[a]nything to the contrary contained in paragraph (1) or (2) … notwithstanding"*, an LLC member / S-corp shareholder / partner gets **$25,000** even when MFJ, and its "portion of the income on which such tax was actually paid" proviso is a limit the app cannot verify, so it needs a KEYED assertion. 17 tests pinning the statute's presence in the brief and the two verify-first findings against the seeded database. ⚠ The content tests **strip markdown** before comparing — blockquote markers and emphasis fall INSIDE the quoted phrases, so a naive search would pass or fail on reformatting rather than on content. ⚠ MOVEMENT: **NONE** — no production code changed. ⛔ **#2 IS NOT FINISHED**: model, lane, compute, render and diagnostics all remain.

## 🟢 **s241t (2026-08-10 — GA QEE CREDIT: the MODEL and the STATUTE, legs 2-3 of 6)** (one deploy; `ce8fd6b`; migrations 0285 + 0286 RLS). **⚠⚠ THE MODEL IS SHAPED BY THE TWO CARRYFORWARD REGIMES.** §48-7-29.16(e) now allows an unused credit against *"up to its **succeeding three years'** tax liability"*, the pre-amendment text said *"the **succeeding five years'**"*, and **2024 Ga. Laws 598 §1-7, eff. 1/1/2025, applies "only to unused tax credits generated during taxable years beginning on or after 1/1/2025"** — so `GeorgiaCredit.source_year` is the discriminator, **never a remaining-years countdown**, which could not survive a rollover. Both edges are pinned (2024 → 5 years, 2025 → 3) and so is the counter-intuitive consequence that falls out of them: **the OLDER credit outlives the newer one** — 2024 runs to 2029 while 2025 runs only to 2028. *That inversion is exactly what a single constant would smooth over, and the error would not surface until a pool expired early or late, years after the mistake.* ⚠ An unknown `source_year` returns **None, not a default**, and the sign cuts both ways: a confident "not expired" lets a dead pool keep reducing Georgia tax, a confident "expired" throws away a live credit — so the caller refuses. **ONE ROW PER CERTIFICATE**, which is the item's whole point: Georgia issues a numbered certificate per approved contribution and a taxpayer may hold several, of different codes and different generation years. A **conditional** unique constraint on (return, certificate number) refuses the same certificate twice — ⚠ and the consumer was checked first (the s241/s241b pair): the compute ITERATES and SUMS these rows, so a duplicate **DOUBLE-COUNTS** rather than vanishing; loud, but still a wrong Georgia credit. Blank certificate numbers are exempt, because the field is optional and several unkeyed rows are legitimate. **⚠ §(b)(3) IS AN OVERRIDE, NOT A FOURTH FILING STATUS**: *"[a]nything to the contrary contained in paragraph (1) or (2) … notwithstanding"* means a MARRIED COUPLE who are S-corp shareholders get **$25,000**, not $5,000 — reading it as a status would cap them at the joint limit, an **UNDERSTATED** credit and the direction nobody reports. **⚠⚠ MFS IS NOT NAMED BY THE STATUTE AND IS REFUSED**: §(b) enumerates *"a single individual or a head of household"* and *"a married couple filing a joint return"*, and neither describes a separate filer — so the cap is UNKNOWN (not half of MFJ, not equal to single), `cap_for` returns None, and the caller refuses. *Guessing there is precisely what the 404-STOP gate exists to prevent.* **⚠ THE REPORTED PACKET CANNOT TEST THE CAP, and that is now a test in its own right**: MFJ with $5,000 expended sits **exactly AT** the (b)(2) limit, so the filed figures agree with an uncapped reading too (s219 — a value that agrees by luck); every cap assertion uses a case where the cap actually binds. ⚠ Series-100 codes are an **OPEN ENUM** with dozens of members, so only code 125 computes and every other code present is **REPORTED BY NAME** rather than silently run through the wrong statute (s235 + s236). ⚠ The federally-deducted total is the figure the Schedule 1 addback is **RECONCILED** against — never written into `S1-5`, *"Add: **other** additions"*, a shared preparer line whose first writer must not become its owner (s230). ⚠ Attached to the **FEDERAL** return like every other document family: a certificate is a taxpayer-level fact that exists whether or not a GA-500 has been attached, and detaching one must not lose it. ⚠ **`compute_ga_qee` WRITES NOTHING** — GA-500 line 21 stays preparer-keyed, because the `500` spec types it `input` and deriving it means re-authoring that spec rather than diverging silently (s142). Also **flipped** s241s's deliberately-inverted test (it asserted the model did NOT exist, so the suite would go red the moment the gap closed — it did). 34 tests; 577 green across the QEE suites and the flow-assertion gate. ⚠ MOVEMENT: **NONE** — two new tables and a pure-function module nothing calls yet; migrations additive. ⛔ **#2 IS NOT FINISHED**: lane, render and diagnostics remain.

## 🟢 **s241u (2026-08-10 — GA QEE CREDIT: the LANE and the DIAGNOSTICS, legs 4 + 6 of 6 — every rule RECONCILES, none WRITES)** (one deploy; no migration). **The lane**: `georgia_credits`, one record per CERTIFICATE, with the IT-QEE-TP2 facts as a nested `qee_detail` dict (the `form_7203` OneToOne shape) — **REFUSED on any credit code but 125**, because every other series-100 credit has its own supporting form with its own fields. ⚠ **The generator emits the nested detail IN THE SAME CHANGE** — it drifted twice before (`schedule_fs.other_expenses` s227, `form_4547s.children` s241q), each time leaving a payload author's own validator rejecting files the server accepted; a test reads the generator's own `defs` to hold the pin. **Staging refuses**: a blank credit code; **a missing `source_year` whenever there is credit to carry** (⚠⚠ ASKED FOR, NEVER DEFAULTED — Georgia runs two carryforward periods at once, so either default is wrong for one of the two populations and the error would surface YEARS later when a pool expired early or late); used > generated + carried-in; a transfer on code 125 (§48-7-29.16 permits none — but ALLOWED on other codes, which ARE transferable, so the refusal is code-specific on purpose); tentatively-allowed > preapproved (the commissioner may PRORATE a request, and the approval is the ceiling); a contribution that PREDATES its approval notice (⚠ a LATE one stages — the 60-day window is an administrative outcome the app should not adjudicate from two keyed dates, so it belongs to the diagnostic); and GA-500 line 21 / S1-5 / every derived figure **refused BY NAME**, each message saying where the value belongs (s238). **Eight diagnostics, and the shape of the whole set is that EVERY RULE RECONCILES AND NONE WRITES** — line 21 and S1-5 are preparer-keyed lines the `500` spec types as `input`, and S1-5 is *"Add: **other** additions"*, SHARED (s230): `D_GAQEE_CODE` (warning — an unmodelled series-100 code NAMED; the amount still reduces Georgia tax as filed, what the app cannot do is check it) · `D_GAQEE_EXPIRED` (error — **the message names WHICH regime it applied**, three years or five; silent on an unknown generation year, because a confident "expired" throws away a live credit) · `D_GAQEE_CAP` (error — the $25,000 pass-through arm read as the OVERRIDE it is) · `D_GAQEE_MFS` (warning — **no cap is asserted** for a filing status the statute does not name, and the message says the software "deliberately not guessed") · `D_GAQEE_L21` (warning — fires only when BOTH sides are non-zero: a keyed line with no certificates is "detail not entered yet", not a contradiction, and firing on it trains people to ignore the rule) · `D_GAQEE_ADDBACK` (error — ⚠⚠ **compared with `<`, NOT `!=`**: S1-5 legitimately carries MORE than the QEE figure whenever any other Georgia addition exists, so a `!=` test would fire on every such return; sign: UNDERSTATES Georgia income — the same dollars taking both a federal deduction and a Georgia credit, which is the entire point of §48-7-29.16(h)(1)) · `D_GAQEE_60DAY` (warning — prompts, never rules) · `D_GAQEE_CERT` (info — a row missing the certificate number the duplicate check needs or the generation year the expiry check needs). **Teeth proven by injection before being trusted** (s232): the `<`-vs-`!=` addback comparison, the both-sides-nonzero line-21 guard, **the generation-year branch (a flat three-year constant would expire a LIVE 2020 pool)**, the 60/61-day boundary, and the pass-through override against the joint cap; every rule also tested QUIET (s241o — only the quiet case proves a comparison is real). 45 lane/diagnostic tests + 34 model/compute + 17 brief. ⚠ MOVEMENT: **NONE** — everything no-ops unless the return carries a `GeorgiaCredit` row, and none exists until a preparer or payload makes one; the published-schema change is additive. ⛔ **#2 IS NOT FINISHED**: the render leg remains (the GA Schedule 2 grid + IT-QEE-TP2 — neither is in `forms_manifest.json`, and both are Georgia DOR PDFs, so check for AcroForm widgets before choosing the backend; ## 🟢 **s225 part 1 (2026-08-07 — KEN RULING: the Schedule L line 24d BOOK BRIDGE ratified and authored into Rule Studio)** (app `2a959a5`; RS `d53da62`; no migration). ## 🟢 **s224 part 2 (2026-08-07 — 1040 LANE: NZ #4 Form 8889/HSA through the IMPORT LANE + Form 8889 LINE 4 BUILT; the NZ list goes 6 → 7 of 10)** (`804b088`; migration 0265 — one column on an EXISTING table, so no RLS migration). **⚠⚠ THE SAME FINDING AS NZ #9 ONE ITEM EARLIER, AND THIS TIME THE SOURCE BRIEF SHOWS WHY.** `HSAAccount`, `compute_8889` (Parts I–III → Schedule 1 lines 13 and 8f, Schedule 2 lines 17c and 17d), eight diagnostics and `SlateForm8889Screen` all shipped Phase 2 on 2026-06-14; the **back-entry lane had no `hsa_accounts` section**, so no packet carrying a Form 8889 could be imported and the form was unreachable from the import path entirely. **The brief's own build plan never named that leg** — its `input` step reads "an 'HSA (8889)' tab + HSA CRUD", which is the BROWSER lane. **THE TWO LANES ARE SEPARATE LEGS, SO A FORM'S BUILD PLAN CAN BE FULLY TICKED WHILE THE FORM STAYS UN-IMPORTABLE** — twice in a row on this list now, and worth writing into every future source brief. Every editable column is importable here, because nothing on this model is engine-written: it is all printed source facts, **including the RED-deferred line 10 (IRA→HSA funding distribution) and line 18 (testing-period failure) amounts**, so a packet's facts survive even where the math stays manual. **⚠⚠ THE ONE REAL COMPUTE GAP — FORM 8889 LINE 4, AND THE SIGN IS THE WHOLE POINT.** `owner_lines` carried the literal `line5 = line3  # line 4 (Archer) = 0`: no column, no input, no diagnostic. Verified against the **2025** Form 8889 (`irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f8889--2025.pdf`) — line 4 is "the amount you and your employer contributed to your Archer MSAs for 2025 from Form 8853, lines 1 and 2", and **line 5 = line 3 − line 4**. Omitting it left line 5 at the full line 3, so the contribution limit came out **too LARGE** and the deduction could exceed §223(b)(4)(A). **AN OMISSION IS ONLY SAFE WHEN IT ERRS AGAINST THE TAXPAYER; THIS ONE DID NOT** — the s221 lesson, again. Now `archer_msa_contributions`, floored at zero per the face's "If zero or less, enter -0-". **⚠ A NEW PARAMETER HAS TO REACH ITS OTHER CALLER**: `D_8889_EXCESS` calls `hsa_deduction` POSITIONALLY to price the 6% excess-contribution warning, so leaving it unupdated would have kept it measuring against the old, too-large limit and contributions that are now excess would go unflagged — pinned by a test that ties the two together. An 8th diagnostic `D_8889_ARCHER` names **Form 8853, which is still NOT BUILT**, rather than letting silence imply zero. **⚠ NO MOVEMENT CLASS**: the column defaults to 0 and the new parameter defaults to 0, so every existing return and every existing caller computes exactly as before. **Two staging warnings ride with the new section**: line 6 is **THREE-STATE and its two "empty" values do OPPOSITE things** — omitted/null takes the full line 5 while an explicit **0** zeroes the whole deduction (`D_8889_FAMILY_ZERO`, the $8,550 → $0 swing from s137) and the diagnostic only fires AFTER commit, so a transcriber typing 0 for "no split" loses the deduction silently; and **line 9 IS the W-2 box 12 code-W total**, so a payload carrying both and disagreeing has one of them mistranscribed and the return can reconcile on wages while still deducting the wrong amount. Regression target met verbatim (`test_form8889_nz4_s224.py`, 14 tests): family HDHP, $3,250 employer contribution, $4,592 distributed against $4,592 of qualified medical expenses → a **$5,300** deduction on Schedule 1 line 13, **zero** taxable distribution and **zero** HSA additional tax of either kind — with the deduction proved **above-the-line by reading 1040 line 11**, not just line 13. All four existing 8889 legs + the s142 backlog green (102); flow assertions + the full back-entry lane green (692); client 14 tests; typecheck 127 = baseline. **⚠ Client note: the Slate 8889 fixture is cast `as HSAAccountRow`, so a NEW REQUIRED FIELD DOES NOT FAIL THE TYPECHECK** — it silently reads `undefined`; kept in step by hand. **⛔ For Ken: Form 8853 is not built** and the 8889's own face says to complete it first when required. **▶ NEXT: NZ #5 Schedule F and #6 SS lump-sum election — ⚠ VERIFY FIRST, both prior items were lane-only gaps on forms that were already built** (`compute_schedule_f.py`, `rules_schedule_f.py` and `_schedule_f_source_brief.md` all exist), then the mixed-entity pilot #7.

## 🟢 **s224 part 1 (2026-08-07 — 1040 LANE: NZ #9 Form 1099-G through the IMPORT LANE; the NZ list goes 5 → 6 of 10)** (`e1a97ac`; migration 0264 — three columns on an EXISTING table, so no RLS migration). The 1120-S queue was empty at boot, so the loop stayed in the 1040 lane and took the top open NZ item by that file's own recommended order. **⚠⚠ THE ITEM WAS MOSTLY ALREADY BUILT — and this is the SECOND time an NZ item described a full form build where only the lane was missing.** "Add 1099-G unemployment documents" reads like a unit; verified against shipped code, the `Form1099G` model, `compute_1099g` (box 1 → Schedule 1 line 7, netting a same-year repayment and printing the "Repaid" literal), the box-4 → 1040 line 25b withholding roster, five diagnostics and `SlateForm1099GScreen` all shipped in **Phase 2 on 2026-06-14**. The one missing leg was the **lane**: `backentry.v1` had no 1099-G section at all, so no packet with unemployment could be back-entered — precisely the blocker the item observed. New section `g_1099s` in all four registries; **schema growth only, zero compute change.** **Box 2 is deliberately NOT importable** — it is the STATE_REFUND worksheet's input and an importable box 2 would double-count Schedule 1 line 1, so its ABSENCE is pinned by a test rather than left to be "completed" later. **⚠⚠ A THIRD DEFECT IN THE GA-500 LINE-24 ROSTER — the one s222 already fixed twice — and its cause is a NEW GENERAL PATTERN: A MISSING COLUMN GETS READ AS A MISSING BOX.** `_populate_ga500_from_federal` added **every** 1099-G's box-11 state withholding to Georgia line 24 **UNGATED**, on the strength of a comment in that very method asserting the form "has no state-code box". It has one — **box 10a State** — on Form 1099-G **Rev. March 2024**, the revision that reports CY2025 (verified by downloading `irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099g--2024.pdf` and reading the face). The column had simply never been stored, **even though `_1099g_source_brief.md` said boxes 10a/10b/11 would all be "stored"** — so a promise in a brief was mistaken for a fact about the form, and every sibling arm of that roster (W-2, 1099-R, 1099-INT/DIV, W-2G, 1099-MISC) was gated on its own state code while this lone exception credited any state's withholding to Georgia and inflated the refund. ## 🟢 **s223 (2026-08-06 — 1040 LANE: BATCH-046 #1 Form 1310 BUILT — BATCH 046 CLOSED)** (`658915e`; migrations 0262 + 0263, a new table and its default-deny RLS ALTER per the new-table rule). Both 1040 batches are now closed. **Form 1310 (Statement of Person Claiming Refund Due a Deceased Taxpayer) did not exist in any form** — no model, serializer, screen, renderer, MeF mapper, diagnostic or lane section — so a return could reconcile to the dollar while silently lacking the claim that entitles anyone to the refund. Built end to end: `Form1310` + `form_1310.py` (the who-must-file gate + the refusal list) + `rules_1310.py` (5 diagnostics) + the AcroForm render + `build_irs1310` + CRUD + the `form_1310s` lane section + `SlateForm1310Screen`. **THE WORK WAS MOSTLY ABOUT REFUSING CORRECTLY, NOT COMPUTING — almost every rule on this form is a REJECT rule.** **No RS spec exists (`1310`/`F1310`/`FORM_1310` all 404), and that is the HOUSE PATTERN for a form with no arithmetic: `8879`, `2848`, `9465` and `8888` all 404 the same way, while `3115` — which computes a §481(a) adjustment — has one.** So the authority is **Form 1310 (Rev. December 2025)**, `IRS1310.xsd` and the `F1310-*` / `IND-298/299/300` business rules, recorded in `specs/_1310_source_brief.md` — **and the business rules turned out to BE the specification: several settle questions the printed face leaves open, and two contradict what the face alone would suggest.** **⚠⚠ BOX A CAN NEVER BE E-FILED**: `IRS1310.xsd` carries the line-A element **commented out** ("not used for e-file at this time") and Part I is a strict `CourtOrPersonalRepGrp` XOR `RefundClaimWithProofOfDeathGrp` choice with no third branch — which fits, because box A asks the IRS to REISSUE a paper check already received in both names, mailed back marked VOID, and is not a claim made on a return at all. It prints; composition refuses it and `build_irs1310` RAISES rather than emitting a schema-invalid document, and a test re-reads the XSD so a future schema drop that enables line A breaks the test instead of silently outliving the refusal. **⚠⚠ BOX B IS VALID ONLY ON AN AMENDED OR SUPERSEDED RETURN** (F1310-024-02 — the face limits it to a claim on Form 1040-X or Form 843) and needs a court-certificate attachment (F1310-023-03); on an ORIGINAL return a court-appointed representative attaches the certificate and files no Form 1310 at all. **⚠⚠ BOX C HAS EXACTLY ONE E-FILEABLE ANSWER SET** — 2a=No, 2b=No, 3=Yes (F1310-009/010/011). The paper face PERMITS the others and explains what follows from each ("the personal representative must file for the refund"; "a refund cannot be made until you submit a court certificate"), so those are legitimate paper returns: the app prints them and refuses the transmission with the rule cited. That also settles a schema question — 2b is REQUIRED by the XSD even though the face says to answer it only when 2a is No. **⚠⚠ TWO TRAPS BURIED IN SCHEMA COMMENTS**: the claimant's NAME is not on Form 1310 in MeF at all ("Refund Claimant Name - Use 'InCareOfNm' from the Return Header"; F1310-019 makes a missing header value a reject, so the document carries only the name CONTROL and the SSN), and `ValidProofOfDeathInd` is REQUIRED inside the box-C group but is **not a box on the printed face** — e-file demands an assertion the paper form never collects. **⚠ THE GATE IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS**: IND-300-01 and IND-298-01 are both conditioned on a NONZERO REFUND and the form exists to *claim* a refund, so a balance-due decedent return needs no Form 1310 — firing there would be an unclearable error on a return that owes money (the s199 class). A court certificate on the return also discharges it, and a surviving spouse filing a JOINT return must not file one at all. **⚠⚠ TWO GAPS FOUND WHILE BUILDING, NEITHER IN THE ITEM: (1) `taxpayer_date_of_death`, `spouse_date_of_death` and `in_care_of` were NOT in the `backentry.v1` allowlist at all — a deceased taxpayer's return could not be back-entered, which made this whole gate UNREACHABLE through the lane (the dates also drive the printed "Died" literal, MeF's PrimaryDeathDt/SpouseDeathDt and IND-424); (2) `_in_care_of_name` already RAISED on any non-MFJ decedent return — "needs a personal-representative name, which the app does not capture yet" — and the Form 1310 claimant IS that name, so this unit CLOSES A PRE-EXISTING E-FILE REFUSAL.** One hypothesis chased and **REFUTED before any code was written**: IND-424 (MFJ + a death date requires `SurvivingSpouseInd`) looked unhandled, which would have rejected every MFJ decedent return — it is a DIFFERENT element on the 1040 signature block and `builder.py` already emits it correctly. The decedent's name, date of death and SSN are **DERIVED from the return, never keyed** (F1310-002/004/008 compare them against it, so a stored copy could only drift into a reject), and a unique constraint on (return, decedent) enforces `maxOccurs="2"` and F1310-005 structurally. Part II answers are tri-state — unanswered ≠ No, which is what Part II genuinely is on a box-A/B form. The field map is derived POSITIONALLY from the template's own geometry and asserted that way, and **the Part III signature and its Date have NO widget at all** (wet ink by design; `f1_14` aligns with "Phone no. (optional)", not the Date) — pinned so nobody "fixes" it by inventing a mapping. Tests: **26** `test_form1310_b046.py` + **9** staging + **3** commit; regression green across 1099-MISC, the diagnostics registry, seed safety, the full back-entry lane (160), MeF composition and the renderer/field-map validators; manifest trip-wire re-pinned 98 → 99; client typecheck 127 = the s220 baseline. **BATCH 046 CLOSED** (#1 built s223, #2–#10 s212), annexed and filed to `CC Code Changes Done` — **both 1040 batches are now closed**. **▶ NEXT: the NZ list — #4 Form 8889/HSA · #5 Schedule F · #6 SS lump-sum election · #9 1099-G unemployment**, then the mixed-entity pilot #7 (the K-1 basis/at-risk allowed-loss worksheet).

## 🟢 **s222 (2026-08-06 — 1040 LANE: BATCH-047 #13 Form 1099-MISC BUILT — BATCH 047 CLOSED)** (`d885ab7`; migrations 0260 + 0261, a new table and its default-deny RLS ALTER per the new-table rule). The 1120-S queue was empty at boot, so the loop stayed in the 1040 lane and closed its last open batch-047 item. **Form 1099-MISC had no model, no import section and no source-level representation anywhere** — the only treatment was a flat Schedule 1 line 8z amount that discarded the payer name, payer TIN, box identity, owner and withholding. Built end to end: `Form1099Misc` + `compute_1099misc.py` + `rules_1099misc.py` (10 diagnostics) + `seed_form_1099misc` + serializer/CRUD + the `misc_1099s` `backentry.v1` section + `SlateForm1099MiscScreen` + its nav tab. **THE AUTHORITY IS THE FORM, NOT A SPEC — and that is the house rule, not a shortcut: `1099MISC` 404s in Rule Studio and so do `1099INT`, `1099DIV`, `1099R`, `1099NEC`, `1099G` and `W2`. No information return is specced there**, so this follows the Form 1099-G precedent and ships `server/specs/_1099misc_source_brief.md`, written from **Form 1099-MISC Rev. April 2025** (the revision that reports CY2025) and its own "Instructions for Recipient". **⚠ THE BOX LAYOUT IS NOT STABLE ACROSS YEARS, and getting the revision right mattered**: on Rev. 4-2025 **box 14 reads "Reserved for future use"** — Rev. 1-2024's "Excess golden parachute payments" was removed (proved by text-extracting all three PDFs: "parachute" appears on five pages of the 2024 file and nowhere in the 2025 one) — while Rev. 12-2026 makes 13a/13b/14 Cash tips / TTOC / Overtime. Box 14 is therefore refused by the lane, and the TY2026 columns exist on the model so the facts are never dropped but are not routed (`D_1099MISC_TY26BOX`, which also says the boxes do not exist on a TY2025 form). **THE DESIGN TURNS ON ONE POINT: only boxes 3 + 8 (→ Schedule 1 line 8z) and box 4 (→ 1040 line 25b) are additive engine feeders.** Every other box reports on an activity's own schedule — Schedule C gross receipts already include boxes 1/5/6/10/11, Schedule E lines 3/4 already include boxes 1/2, Schedule F line 6a already includes box 9 — so routing them again would **double count**, the exact failure the item itself names. A row routed to an activity is therefore **traceability, not a feeder**: it carries the FK, the payer record survives, and `D_1099MISC_RECON` catches the *opposite* error instead — an activity keyed for LESS than the 1099-MISC routed to it, which nothing on the return caught before. **⚠ SCHEDULE 1 LINE 8z ALREADY HAD AN OWNER**: `compute_state_refund_db` writes AND blanks it, so two unconditional writers would fight and the state-refund disengage path would erase a 1099-MISC amount (the s221 "one number, many surfaces" class). 8z is now **composed by a single final writer** that reads the worksheet's share back from the row the worksheet itself owns; disengage hands the line back rather than blanking it, and a displaced direct entry is recorded **once, on the not-engaged → engaged transition** so `D_1099MISC_8Z` reports it — recomputing that marker would compare the composed figure against itself, agree, and let the preparer's entry vanish on the second recompute (pinned as a test). Box 4 and box 16 join their **existing** rosters rather than being written here. **E-file: there is no `IRS1099MISC` element anywhere in the 1040 MeF schema set** (2025v5.3 and v5.4 both grepped — IRS1099R, IRSW2 and IRSW2G are the only information-return documents), so a 1099-MISC does not transmit as a document and no builder was written; likewise no render leg, since it is an input document. **⚠⚠ TWO LIVE DEFECTS FOUND WHILE BUILDING, NEITHER REPORTED, both in the GA-500 line-24 withholding roster this item had to join anyway: (1) it read `g.state_withholding`, which DOES NOT EXIST on `Form1099G` (the column is `box11_state_withholding`), so `_populate_ga500_from_federal` raised `AttributeError` on ANY return carrying a 1099-G row — a 500 on the GA-500 federal pull for every Georgia return with unemployment income; (2) `FormW2G` was missing from that roster entirely, so Georgia withholding on a W-2G never reached line 24.** Both fixed and pinned; (2) is a movement class — GA-500 line 24 and the Georgia refund rise on any existing return with a GA-withheld W-2G. Also guarded the three activity FKs against pointing at another return's activity (DRF's generated `PrimaryKeyRelatedField` queries the whole table). Tests: **21** `test_form1099misc_b047.py` + **6** staging + **5** commit + **17** Slate; regression green across the 1099-G legs, the whole back-entry lane (148), Schedule A, state refund, the GA-500 pull family, the diagnostics registry and the flow assertions. ## 🟢 **s200 (2026-08-04, same day — 046 #9 REFUTED AT THE PRESCRIBED LAYER: the server never dropped the home-office election; the Slate CHECKBOX was lying during the save round trip)** (`1490437`, pushed → deploy; NO migration; client-only). Adopted at all 3 checkbox sites on SlateScheduleCScreen. Revert-proved (the pin fails on the old checkbox at exactly the snap-back assertion); live-verified on the subject return — line 30 $1,000 · Sch C net $20,591 · AGI $19,680, the item's exact expected values, surviving entry, navigation and hard reload. ⚠ Class remains: 47 other Slate screens hand-roll bare checkboxes (88 sites) and tri-state SELECTS have the same gap — sweep in DEFERRAL_AUDIT. ## 🔴 s105 ADDENDUM — **THE RENDER DEPLOY HAD BEEN BROKEN SINCE s104; NOTHING FROM s104 OR s105 WAS EVER LIVE.** Ken pasted the deploy log: `build.sh` → `manage.py seed_all` → `-> seed_backfill_returns` → `Build failed 😞`. `seed_all` DISCOVERS every command named `seed_*` and runs it **with no arguments against production**; s104's `seed_backfill_returns` is not a form seeder at all — it takes a required `folder` positional pointing at roster CSVs that exist only on Ken's machine. ## 🟢 **s145 (2026-07-30): KEN'S BACKLOG — LEG 2 ITEM 4 COMPLETE (`3850e2d` on `slate-ui`, NO DEPLOY).** **KEN RULED on the education-credit election, and the item is built.** §25A(c)(2)(A) forbids one student taking BOTH education credits, but it is an **ELECTION** — the LLC is barred only *"if the taxpayer **elects** to have [the AOTC] apply with respect to such individual"* — so "drop the LLC wherever the AOTC is allowed" would impose an election nobody made. **Ken's ruling: a nonzero AOTC amount on an AOTC-eligible student IS the election** (`compute_8863.aotc_elected`), and that student leaves the line-10 LLC base. Entering $0 AOTC is how a preparer chooses LLC-only; an ineligible student cannot elect at all, so their LLC expenses stand. **The same $4,000 can no longer earn both credits — $800 on the s138 proof return.** Ken considered and rejected an explicit per-student election field (a migration + one more box) and leaving compute alone behind the blocking error. Ruling recorded in **DECISIONS.md**. ⚠⚠ **`D_8863_DUAL_STUDENT` DEMOTED error → warning** — s142 promoted it only because compute did not enforce the rule; it does now, so nothing is left to block, and `warning` is the severity the RS spec carries. The message names the student, the dollars on BOTH sides and which credit the student was put on, so the election is never silent. ⚠⚠ **The app is now knowingly AHEAD of a SECOND spec** — `R-8863-LLC` sums every student's LLC expenses with no §25A(c)(2)(A) exclusion, and the spec KNOWS the rule (it carries a warning diagnostic) but never as a COMPUTATION. Fetched live (key `FORM_8863`) and diffed against the cached copy — identical but for the export timestamp. Flagged in REVIEW_QUEUE **with the PATTERN named: three forms (5329, 8863, Schedule 1-A) now diverge in the same direction, their specs carrying the arithmetic but not the statutory exception — one conversation, not three tickets.** ⚠⚠ **THE FIRST DRAFT OF THE NEW TEST SUITE COULD NOT SEE ITS OWN REGRESSION** — its helper re-derived the two bases with `aotc_elected` instead of reading what `compute_8863_db` wrote, so reverting the fix left every test in the file passing. It now runs a real `compute_return` and reads FORM_8863 lines 1 and 10. **A test that re-implements the thing it tests is blind by construction.** Both fixes revert-tested (4 and 3 failures). Gates: new suite **12** · flow assertions **521** (baseline exactly) · 8863 / Topic 8 / Sch 3 / MeF-1040 bands **298**. No migration; `seed_rules` on BOTH DBs at deploy (a SEVERITY change — it lives in two places, the s109b lesson). ▶ NEXT: **LEG 2 item 5** — the Schedule 1-A tips owner filter. *(PAUSED in s146 — Ken redirected to the redesign.)*

## 🟢 **s143 (2026-07-30): KEN'S BACKLOG — LEG 2 ITEMS 1 + 2 COMPLETE (`4c76624` on `slate-ui`, pushed, NO DEPLOY).** The first compute fixes of the backlog. **8 new tests, every fix revert-tested, no migration, no seed change, no client change** — compute-only, so it needs nothing at deploy beyond the push. ⭐ **(1) ITEM 1 — the stale QBI deduction on 1040 line 13 ($859 understated).** `compute_8995_db`'s not-engaged branch left line 13 alone on the stated grounds that "a direct entry survives", but line 13 is a COMPUTED line (`seed_1040`: `is_computed=True`), so a genuine preparer figure is an OVERRIDE and `write_line_13`'s `is_overridden` guard already protected it. What the old branch actually preserved was residue: delete the last §199A source and the deduction it produced stayed for ever, still reducing taxable income, and recomputing never cleared it. Now `blank_form_rows() + write_line_13("")`, which pops `values["13"]` so the 14/15 reflow recovers the taxable income in the same pass. **The fix FOLLOWS the RS spec rather than diverging** — `R-8995-L15` makes 1040 line 13a the Form 8995 line-15 figure, so with no line 15 the line is blank. ⚠⚠ **NEW FINDING, never previously logged: it was an E-FILE defect too.** 1040 line 13 maps to `QualifiedBusinessIncomeDedAmt` in `builder.py`'s `LINE_ORDER`, and the builder OMITS a blank line from the XML while emitting a stored one — so the stale figure was **transmitted** as a real QBI deduction with the Form 8995 rows blank, a deduction claimed with no supporting form behind it. Lesson banked: **follow a defective line into E-FILE, not just into print.** ⭐ **(2) ITEM 2 — the `disengage()`-guarded-on-`!= ZERO` family, and the ROOT CAUSE was narrower than the backlog assumed.** The guard was the symptom; the cause was that `compute_8863_db` wrote the nonrefundable credit to Schedule 3 line 3 **unconditionally** while the refundable half FIVE LINES UP already wrote `""` at zero — two writes in the same function disagreeing. So the one value the engaged path could produce (a credit phased out / MFS-barred / with no qualifying expenses stores a literal `"0"`) was the one value the clear-up refused to touch, surviving the deletion of every student. Fixed at BOTH ends. ⚠ **The instructed "sweep the family" was AUDITED, not assumed, and the honest answer is that the other three were LATENT, not defective** — `compute_1116` writes `""` when its credit is `<= 0`, and `compute_8960` / `compute_2210` call `disengage()` outright when their amounts are `<= 0`, so none could ever write the zero its guard refused to clear; reporting four live bugs would have been false. All three hardened anyway, with `test_sibling_modules_never_write_a_zero_feeder` **pinning the reason each is safe**. Every guard now detects the change through the write itself, so an already-blank row costs nothing and no longer fires a pointless `compute_sch_2/3` reflow. No dollar moves on item 2 — a blank and a "0" sum identically. 🔴 **ITEM 4 (one student taking BOTH education credits, $800) was DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT and is escalated to Ken.** The spec fetch (the CLAUDE.md gate) found that `R-8863-LLC` says outright *"L10 = Σ student LLC adjusted expenses"* with no §25A(c)(2)(A) exclusion — the spec carries the same defect, and only knows the rule as a *warning diagnostic*, never as a computation (the item-3 `R-5329-02` shape again). Worse, **§25A(c)(2)(A) is an ELECTION** — it bars the LLC only *"if the taxpayer elects"* the AOTC for that student — so the backlog's one-line framing would have compute silently pick one credit over another. ## 🟢 **s141 (2026-07-30), unit 25: FORM 5329 / ADDITIONAL TAXES ON QUALIFIED PLANS (Parts I-IX) SHIPPED (`slate-ui`, no deploy).** **DOCUMENT TABS PER OWNER** — here the "one form per owner" ruling is literal: taxpayer and spouse each file a separate Form 5329, printed as its own copy and transmitted as its own e-file document. Inside a tab the nine parts are InputRow worksheets, the five excess-contribution parts share ONE generated block (same shape: a prior-year carryforward reduced by absorbing amounts, plus the current year's excess, taxed at 6% of the smaller of that total or the 12/31 account value), and the whole computed face renders from the server's own per-owner line dict as locked ƒx cells. ⚠ **THIS UNIT MADE ONE SERVER CHANGE, ADDITIVE AND READ-ONLY:** `Form5329Serializer.computed_lines` / `.computed_total` now expose the SAME `compute_5329_form_lines` dict the diagnostics, the renderer and the MeF extract already consume. It was necessary, not cosmetic — **no API published this form's arithmetic at all** (`compute_5329_db` persists only the TAXPAYER's Part I lines 1-4 to FormFieldValue, and Schedule 2 line 8 holds BOTH owners combined), which is exactly why the legacy screen re-implemented all seven part formulas itself in `previewIItoIX`; the sweep's standing ruling (units 17 and 19) is to RETIRE client re-implementations of the engine, not carry them forward. No migration; 7 new server tests; the 91 existing Topic-5 / 5329 / seed-leg tests still green. **SIX REAL DEFECTS:** ⚠⚠⚠ (1) **THE 25% SIMPLE RATE IS CHARGED ON THE WHOLE OF LINE 3, NOT THE SIMPLE PORTION.** The Part I caution on the 2025 form face reads "If any part of the amount on line 3 was a distribution from a SIMPLE IRA, you may have to include 25% of **that amount** on line 4 instead of 10%" — 25% belongs on the SIMPLE slice with 10% on the rest. `compute_5329_full` carries ONE boolean and multiplies the ENTIRE line 3 by it, and the boolean is auto-set from **any** code-S 1099-R on the return (`bool(row.simple_25pct) or has_s`), so the mixed case fires by itself with no preparer action. Engine-proven: 50,000 of code-1 early 401(k) money alongside 2,000 of code-S SIMPLE money gives line 4 = 25% × 52,000 = **13,000** against a correct blend of 10% × 50,000 + 25% × 2,000 = **5,500** — **$7,500 OVERSTATED** — and the distortion GROWS as the SIMPLE slice shrinks: 100,000 + 500 gives **25,125 vs 10,125**, $15,000 overstated. Live-proven on the demo QA return through the real API (line 1 52,000 / line 3 52,000 / line 4 13,000 → Schedule 2 line 8 **23,420**, balance due **47,024**). Direction OVERSTATEMENT — the client overpays. **The RS spec's R-5329-02 carries the same simplification**, so per the authoritative-source rule this is FLAGGED, never silently fixed → REVIEW_QUEUE (split line 1 by code, apportion the line-2 exception, blend the rates, then correct the spec). ⚠⚠ (2) **A BLANK 12/31 ACCOUNT VALUE TAXES THE FULL EXCESS AND AN EXPLICIT 0 TAXES NOTHING.** The six `*_value` fields are the form's only nullable inputs and `_excess_part` reads None as "no smaller-of cap". Live-proven on ONE cell, three states, all through the real API: a 7,000 traditional-IRA excess with the value at 3,000 → **180** of tax; an explicit **0** → **0**; cleared to null → **420**. So the most natural way to record "I don't have the year-end statement" costs the client money, typing 0 quietly asserts an emptied account, and nothing on screen distinguished the three. Six parts blank at once → 1,398. D_5329_003 is only a `warning` → REVIEW_QUEUE (raise to error). ⚠⚠ (3) **THE SCREEN RE-IMPLEMENTED THE ENGINE AND DISPLAYED A NUMBER THAT IS NOT THE 5329 TAX.** `previewIItoIX` duplicated all seven part formulas and deliberately EXCLUDED Part I, then labelled the result "Parts II-IX preview": engine-proven, Part I 2,000 + Parts II-IX 2,920 = an owner total of **4,920** while the screen showed **2,920**. There was also no line 1/3/4 display at all, no per-part result, no owner total and no Schedule 2 line 8. ⚠⚠ (4) **THE PART IX CORRECTION-WINDOW ROW IS WORTH 15 PERCENTAGE POINTS AND THE SCREEN NEVER SAID SO.** SECURE 2.0 §302 charges 10% when the shortfall is corrected inside the correction window and 25% otherwise; engine-proven, the same 40,000 missed RMD costs **4,000** on line 52a and **10,000** on line 52b — a 6,000 swing on which row it is keyed to. The legacy labels named the rows but never defined the window or the stake, and D_5329_004 is only `info`. The waiver route (attach a statement, pay nothing) cannot be expressed by the model at all. ⚠ (5) **THE SIMPLE CHECKBOX CAN READ FALSE WHILE THE ENGINE APPLIES 25%** — a code-S 1099-R forces the rate regardless of the box, so the screen showed an unticked box on a return taxed at 2.5× the displayed rate (live-confirmed). ⚠ (6) **D_RET_007, THE ONE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SAYS "VERIFY THE RATE APPLIED", IS NOT DUAL-AWARE** — it reads the DEPRECATED `Taxpayer.f5329_simple_25pct` scalar and the 1099-R codes, never the per-owner `Form5329.simple_25pct` row field, though `_f5329_state` in the same module is fully dual-aware and every other 5329 diagnostic uses it; ticking the box on the dual model with no code-S document gets the 25% silently, from the exact check written to catch it. Also surfaced at the cell that causes it: a stranded exception on the owner with no early distribution (the 10% is charged in full on the OTHER owner's form, D_5329_001), an exception amount with **no exception number** (the form requires it; nothing checked), an invalid exception number (D_RET_006), Part II line 6 above line 5 (D_5329_002), and a spouse form on a non-joint return. ⚠ **TWO DEFECTS IN THE NEW SCREEN ITSELF, caught by its own tests and its live run:** six excess parts shared ONE `aria-label` per cell ("12/31/2025 account value") — ambiguous to a screen reader and to `getByLabelText` alike — and the blank-cap ERROR PROSE was generic too, so six identical-looking errors could not be told apart; every per-part label and message now names its account.
