**s109 (2026-07-25, autonomous "go" — the top unblocked item): FORM 8879 "PERSISTENCE" FIXED, AND THE SERVER WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG.** Commit `edfca9c`, pushed `47002c3..edfca9c`. **CLIENT-ONLY: zero server source changed, no migrations, no production DB writes.** The QA-ranked P0 the external backlog silently dropped: a preparer started an MFJ Form 8879, keyed both PINs and both signature dates, captured the Part I snapshot, opened Forms (the 8879 WAS in the generated package), came back to Input — and the card read **"Start Form 8879"** with every field blank. **NOTHING WAS EVER LOST, AND THE QA REPORT CARRIED ITS OWN PROOF:** the run's final diagnostics still listed `D_8879_NEED`, and `d_8879_need` returns `[]` when the `Form8879` row is absent — so the row demonstrably survived the navigation that appeared to destroy it. The tester read the surviving warning as evidence of the loss; it was evidence of the opposite. **THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THE SEAM, NOT THE FORM:** a "self-managing" card seeds `useState` from its `initial` prop **once at mount** and thereafter PATCHes the server directly, never telling FormEditor — so `returnData.form_8879` sat at its page-load `null` for the entire session — and the Payments tab is conditionally rendered (`activeTab === "payments" ? <PaymentsSection/>`), so leaving for Forms **unmounts** the card and coming back **remounts** it onto that stale seed. (Clicking "Start Form 8879" again was harmless — the endpoint is `get_or_create`, so the PINs came back — but a preparer seeing a blank card concludes the work is gone, which is exactly what the tester concluded.) **NINE CARDS SHARED THE SHAPE AND ALL NINE ARE FIXED, not just the reported one:** 8879 · 8878 · 4868 · 8888 · 9465 · payment vouchers · 2848 · 3115 · 2553. Each now takes an `onChange` that reports **only what the server confirmed** (a refused PATCH reports nothing, so the parent can never cache a record the DB rejected), and FormEditor's new `setSingleton` records it with an **in-place key write, not a refetch** — none of these cards feeds the 1040 computation from the client, and a refetch would risk stomping unflushed keystrokes elsewhere. **⚠ THE GENERAL LESSON, worth more than the form: a "self-managing" card is only safe while it is MOUNTED.** Anything conditionally rendered must report its server state upward, or its parent's copy becomes a stale seed that silently un-does completed work — and nothing in the existing test suite could see it, because no test ever unmounted and remounted a card mid-session. **Gates:** NEW `singletonCardPersistence.test.tsx` **7** (four of the seven failed before the fix — the reproduction was written first) → **vitest 396** (was 389) · **tsc 0** · NEW `server/tests/test_8879_persistence.py` **7**, which **passed on the FIRST run with no server change** — the cleanest available proof that the DB half was never broken; it pins the hard-reload payload, the **`?fresh_return=1` payload** (that one replaces `returnData` wholesale mid-session, so a missing key there would silently re-stale the seed and reopen the defect), `get_or_create` idempotency, and the diagnostic evidence itself · `test_8879_8878` **33/33** unchanged. **No full server suite run — deliberate** (zero server source changed; the s108e run of 6,192/7/21 stands). **LIVE-VERIFIED ON THE DEMO PROJECT** (`django-demo` → `tts-tax-demo`; production never touched) on John & Judy Jones MFJ 1040 — the same return s94 probed, AGI 35,492: started → Forms → back to Input keeps the card · PINs 54654/16546 + both 07/23/2026 dates + the Part I snapshot survive a **hard reload** AND a second Forms round trip ("within tolerance") · Form 8879 present in the generated package (⚠ it takes ~15s to render — an early check reads as absent) · scratch record deleted, demo left as found. **Two adjacent QA findings filed to `REVIEW_QUEUE.md` rather than changed silently:** (a) **`D_8879_NEED` is a warning no preparer can ever clear** — it fires whenever an 8879 is needed, signed or not, and the actionable gate is the separate `D_8879_UNSIGNED` error; Now attaches on any GA-tagged W-2/1099-R/1099-INT/1099-DIV (the same sources line 24 aggregates withholding from, so attachment and withholding can no longer disagree); **1099-G deliberately excluded** — it has no state-code box, so treating the practice's file-as-GA convention as a CREATE signal would attach Georgia to every return with a state refund, nonresidents included. Derived RIE lines now also follow their source back DOWN (deleting a 1099-R used to leave a stale exclusion and overstate the refund); safe to always-write because saving a field sets `is_overridden=True`. **(4) ONE 1099-R SPLIT INTO SEVERAL PARTIAL RECORDS.** TWO independent create paths (`handleUpdate` and `handlePayerEinBlur`) with NO in-flight guard on either → a POST per blur, each record holding only the field that created it, with the payer lookup enriching whichever one it happened to make; `+ Add 1099-R` separately POSTed a `"New Payer"` placeholder on every click. Now the s107 draft-card shape: no request on click · nothing POSTs until `payer_name` (a non-blank CharField) · values keyed before it ride the single create · `creatingRef` serialises concurrent blurs onto ONE create · the EIN blur funnels through that same path · **enrichment fills BLANKS ONLY** and never overwrites a typed payer name · inline validation keeps the card and its contents · no mid-entry remount · delete awaits any in-flight create. **(5) AUTOSAVE.** `commit()` bundles every dirty field into one PATCH (s105, deliberate) but DRF rejects the WHOLE payload on one bad field, so an invalid PIN discarded the spouse/address/preparer edits riding with it. Now reads DRF's field-level errors, drops only the named fields and retries once with the remainder; the save result grew `boolean` → `{ok, failed[]}` so rejected fields stay dirty while accepted ones clear. Monotonic `factSeqRef` gives latest-write-wins (a slow FAILED save could paint "Save failed" after a newer save had already succeeded). **⚠ A real fragility surfaced while testing:** `settle()` read `formRef`, which was only assigned during RENDER — an already-resolved save runs its `.then` BEFORE React re-renders, so accepted fields stayed dirty; masked in production only by network latency ordering the render first. The mirror is now updated synchronously. **LIVE-VERIFIED ON THE SEPARATE DEMO SUPABASE PROJECT** (`django-demo` launch config → `tts-tax-demo`; production was NEVER touched at any point), with a scratch MFJ retiree since deleted: GA-500 auto-attached from a 1099-R with no W-2 · the Info tab rendered identity with ZERO entity controls · the worksheet showed spouse L11 521 + L12 44,913 → **L17 45,434** and taxpayer L12 61,497 → L17 61,497 with both gates checked from DOB. **45,434 is the Batch-001 answer-key figure, DERIVED from the governing rule rather than fitted to the target** (TaxWise output is a cross-check, never a source). **Gates:** NEW `test_ga500_rie_federal_pull.py` **20** · NEW `stateIndividualInfo.test.tsx` **13** · NEW `retirement1099RDraftRow.test.tsx` **14** · NEW `autosaveValidationIsolation.test.tsx` **7** → **vitest 389** (was 355) · **tsc 0** · GA-500 band + flow assertions **604 passed**. **NO migrations; no production DB writes.** ✅ **FULL SERVER SUITE CONFIRMED (s108e): 6,192 passed / 7 failed / 21 skipped, 55:25** — the 7 are EXACTLY the known pre-existing set (8915f landing ×2 · AAA-negative ×2 · officer-comp ×2 · manifest-json); ## **s107 (2026-07-24, Ken-directed bug fix — the first work inside P1's Schedule D/8949 unit): THE "+ ADD TRANSACTION" BUTTON IS FIXED — Schedule D could not be started at all.** `ScheduleDSection.handleAdd` POSTed `description: ""` the instant the button was clicked; `CapitalTransaction.description` is a non-blank CharField, so DRF answered **400 "This field may not be blank."**, `onRefresh()` re-read an unchanged list, and **no editable row ever appeared** — a dead button on the biggest back-entry unlock (~9 returns). Client-only, ZERO compute code, no migrations, no DB writes. **THE NEW SHAPE:** the click seeds a **client-side draft row** (`SCHD_DRAFT_ID`) held in component state and renders it immediately, fully editable, with NO request; nothing is POSTed until the description is non-blank; columns keyed BEFORE the description accumulate in `draftValuesRef` and are sent WITH it in the single create, so one transaction is always one record. **The duplicate/split guard:** `creatingRef` holds the in-flight create promise, assigned synchronously with the POST's first `await` — any blur landing mid-flight awaits it and PATCHes the id it returns; there is exactly ONE code path that can POST and it is gated on both `draftIdRef` and `creatingRef`, so fast tabbing through six columns can no longer split a lot across two 8949 rows. **Validation is inline** (a note inside the draft card carries the missing-description prompt or the DRF 400 message, `role="alert"`) and the row plus everything typed into it SURVIVE, with the next edit retrying the create. **No mid-entry remount** — once persisted the row keeps rendering AS the draft row (same key, same DOM nodes) with the server row merged in for computed column (h) rather than reappearing as a fresh list row: the s105/s106 lesson that a remount wipes whatever field the preparer had not blurred yet. Delete on an unsaved draft is local-only; on a saved draft it awaits any in-flight create so no record is orphaned. Ordinary-row edit/delete/calculation paths untouched; `ScheduleDSection` exported for testing (the `DueDiligenceAttestation` precedent). **Gates:** NEW `scheduleDDraftRow.test.tsx` **13** (draft appears with zero requests · one record per transaction · pre-description values land on it · gated-promise rapid entry → 1 POST · 400 keeps the row and its values · reload persists · unchanged ordinary-row PATCH path) → **vitest 355** (was 342); NEW `tests/test_schedule_d_draft_row.py` **10** — which pins the API side so the client contract can't drift: the OLD payload still 400s (holding the draft is the only correct behaviour, not a style preference) · one create + PATCHes = 1 row · GET round-trips every column · **gain 3,000 → Sch D line 16 → 1040 line 7, and GA-500 line 8 == 1040 line 11 → Georgia AGI line 10 +3,000** (loss case and PATCH-recompute case too). Flow-assertion gate + Schedule D / 8949 / GA-500 bands re-ran **582 passed**; `tsc` 86 errors before AND after — identical set, all pre-existing. ⚠ **NOT live-verified in a browser**: `server/.env` points dev at the PRODUCTION Supabase project, so a preview click-through writes real `CapitalTransaction` rows to prod; the 13 client tests render the real section and drive real DOM change/blur events instead. ▶ NEXT: **continue P1 — the Schedule D/8949 unit**; the entry layer is now usable, so **audit ENTRY vs COMPUTE for the rest of the form before building** (Topic 9 compute is long-shipped and green — expect more entry-layer gaps like this one, not engine work), then **GA Form 500 RIE** (the 1017 retirement-exclusion mismatch — every retiree). ⚠ **Two deploys await verification**: s106e's 8962 annual method (bundle grep `Line 11 — Annual Calculation`) and s107 (grep the draft-note text `enter a description in column (a)`).

**s105 (2026-07-23, Ken-directed PRIORITY — ADDED to the Spine as S-26, off-spine per the never-silent rule): THE SEVEN ENTRY-LAYER BUGS FROM THE LIVE 1017 BACK-ENTRY PILOT ARE CLOSED (`166e6ef`; mig returns.0209 = a state-only AlterModelOptions; ZERO compute code — flow 518 stands).** **The pilot's headline is that the ENGINE IS RIGHT**: on a real 2025 1040 (wages + interest + two 1099-Rs + Social Security) every line matched TaxWise to the dollar — SS taxability worksheet, the 2025 senior deduction with its MAGI phaseout, the age-65 standard deduction, brackets, withholding aggregation, refund. **Every defect was in the INPUT layer**, and each one is the kind an agent/human fleet mass-produces. **(1) THE 10x AMOUNT-MASK BUG** (Ken: highest priority) — clicking a box showing `0.00` dropped the caret INSIDE the mask, so 25,884 saved as 258,840. NEW `client/src/renderer/lib/selectOnFocus.ts`: ONE delegated `focusin` handler installed at boot selects-all on every amount box (the TaxWise/Lacerte convention) and caps it at 15 chars — a single place to reason about instead of an onFocus prop on ~280 raw inputs, and it covers keyboard/programmatic focus too; a `mouseup` guard re-selects after the click that collapses the caret, and a drag-selection is respected. **(2) CARD LISTS RE-SORTING MID-ENTRY** — the root cause was `Meta.ordering = ["order", <editable name>]` while EVERY card is created with `order=0`, i.e. the list was really sorted ALPHABETICALLY BY PAYER and re-sorted on each keystroke of the name. Adding a 1099-R (the API seeds payer "New Payer") put the new card ABOVE "Teachers Retirement System", so the preparer's next keystrokes landed on the taxpayer's EXISTING card — box 2a became the concatenation 4362511485 and the refund monitor read **$1.68 BILLION**. The tie-break is now the immutable `created_at` on **all eight** document-card models (W-2 · 1099-INT · 1099-DIV · 1099-R · Sch C · Sch C other-expense · Sch F · Sch F other-expense); cards append and STAY PUT. **(3) NUMERIC OVERFLOW → 500** — the columns are wide enough (`max_digits=15`) to STORE the garbage, so DRF's own check never fired and the value reached the compute chain. NEW `MoneyBoundedSerializer` (1040 entry cards + taxpayer facts ONLY — business figures legitimately run to billions) returns **400** at ≥$1,000,000,000 with a per-field message; `api.ts` now NAMES the field in the failed-save banner. **(4) THE FILING-STATUS WIPE** — these cards commit on BLUR but a `<select>` commits on CHANGE, and that save re-seeds every card from the server, so anything typed-but-not-yet-blurred was gone from the screen AND had never reached the DB. `useTaxpayerFacts` now keeps dirty fields across a re-seed AND flushes them alongside whatever is being committed. **(5) DOB** — commits as soon as the date is COMPLETE (not only on blur) + NEW **`D_1040_018`** warning on a missing taxpayer/spouse DOB: on the pilot, blank DOBs silently dropped **$15,200** of age-derived deductions (tax over by $1,824) with no diagnostic at all. **(6) DIAGNOSTIC SIGNAL** — `D_EIC_007` is now **INFO** when the engine auto-resolved it from the DOB (the childless age test), so retiree-with-wages returns stop opening with an unactionable red; it stays an ERROR when the preparer ASSERTED claimed-as-dependent / QC-of-another. `LATE_FILING` is **suppressed** for `rolled_from_source='backfill-2025'` — all ~3,300 shells are late by design. **(7) THE SEEDED-SHELL BANNER** now reads "Seeded for 2025 back-entry", not the false "carried values were copied from the prior-year return"; `BACKFILL_RETURN_SOURCE` is a shared constant on both sides. **PLUS (8) the NEW DEFAULT "Tax Shelter" FOREST THEME** (Ken: "more forest green, less cream") — forest `#1e362a` carries the structure (nav, primary, ink), the canvas moves off cream onto pale green, gold `#a9884f` is a garnish, Georgia serif headings; sampled from the firm's own work in `D:\dev\taxshelter-design`. **Ledger stays in the list unchanged as the one-click rollback**, and the RED/YELLOW/GREEN data-entry convention is untouched as always.
